subject: physics

concepts.title: Weighted Average Atomic Mass
concepts.definition: The atomic mass of a chemical element containing multiple isotopes is calculated as the weighted mean of their individual atomic masses using their natural percentage abundances.
concepts.key_idea: Isotopic abundance determines the natural atomic weight of an element.
question_patterns: find the average atomic mass of an element with two isotopes
calculate the atomic mass given relative percentage abundances
what is the average mass of chlorine given abundance of its isotopes
determine the weighted atomic mass from isotopic percentage distribution
compute the expected atomic mass for a mixture of isotopes

solution_steps.action: multiply isotopic masses by abundances and sum

concepts.title: Composition of Nucleus and Neutron Number
concepts.definition: The count of neutrons in a given nuclide is obtained by subtracting its atomic number from its mass number.
concepts.key_idea: Mass number represents the total nucleon count comprising protons and neutrons.
question_patterns: find the number of neutrons in a nucleus of mass number A and atomic number Z
calculate neutron count for a given nuclide notation
what is the number of neutrons in gold nuclide 197Au79
determine how many neutrons are present in lead 208Pb82
compute the neutron number N from A and Z

solution_steps.action: subtract atomic number from mass number
solution_steps.explain: neutron number equals mass number minus atomic number

concepts.title: Nuclear Radius and Size
concepts.definition: The radius of an atomic nucleus varies directly with the cube root of its mass number, maintaining constant nuclear mass density.
concepts.key_idea: Nuclear radius scales proportionally with the one-third power of mass number.
question_patterns: find the radius of a nucleus given its mass number A
calculate the nuclear size using mass number and R0 constant
what is the nuclear radius of iron nucleus with mass number 56
determine the radius of a heavy nucleus from its mass number
compute nuclear radius using the cube root relationship

solution_steps.action: calculate cube root of mass number

solution_steps.explain: scale by nuclear radius constant r0

concepts.title: Mass Energy Equivalence
concepts.definition: Mass can be converted into an equivalent amount of energy according to relativity theory using the square of the speed of light in vacuum as conversion factor.
concepts.key_idea: Energy released from mass destruction is equal to mass multiplied by speed of light squared.
question_patterns: calculate the energy equivalent of a given mass in kilograms
find the energy liberated when mass m is converted into energy
what is the energy equivalent of 1 gram of matter
determine energy output from mass loss using mass energy relation
compute Joules of energy corresponding to a specified mass

solution_steps.action: multiply mass by speed of light squared

concepts.title: Mass Defect of a Nucleus
concepts.definition: The total mass of isolated constituent protons and neutrons minus the actual rest mass of the bound nucleus defines the mass defect.
concepts.formula: mass_defect = Z * proton_mass + (A - Z) * neutron_mass - nuclear_mass
concepts.key_idea: Formation of a stable nucleus results in a loss of total rest mass.
question_patterns: calculate the mass defect of a nucleus given its atomic and mass numbers
find the difference between constituent nucleon mass and nuclear mass
what is the mass defect of oxygen 16 nucleus
determine mass defect for helium 4 nucleus from constituent masses
compute mass defect in atomic mass units u

solution_steps.action: compute combined mass of all protons
solution_steps.explain: multiply proton count by single proton mass

solution_steps.action: compute combined mass of all neutrons
solution_steps.explain: multiply neutron count by single neutron mass

solution_steps.action: subtract bound nuclear mass from sum of constituent masses
solution_steps.explain: mass defect is constituent sum minus nuclear mass

concepts.title: Nuclear Binding Energy and Binding Energy Per Nucleon
concepts.definition: The binding energy per nucleon represents the mean energy needed to liberate one nucleon from the atomic nucleus.
concepts.key_idea: Higher binding energy per nucleon signifies greater nuclear stability.
question_patterns: find the binding energy per nucleon for a nuclide in MeV
calculate nuclear binding energy per nucleon from mass defect
what is the binding energy per nucleon for nitrogen 14 nucleus
determine average binding energy per nucleon for iron 56
compute binding energy per nucleon given mass defect in u

solution_steps.action: convert mass defect to binding energy in MeV
solution_steps.explain: multiply mass defect in u by 931.5 MeV/u

solution_steps.action: divide total binding energy by mass number

concepts.title: Properties of Strong Nuclear Force
concepts.definition: The fundamental force holding nucleons together is strongly attractive at distances above 0.8 fm, independent of charge, and short-ranged.
concepts.key_idea: Nuclear force dominates over electrostatic repulsion at short range and exhibits saturation.
question_patterns: explain the key characteristics of nuclear force
what are the main properties of the force binding nucleons
state why nuclear forces exhibit saturation property
verify charge independence of nuclear interaction
describe the variation of potential energy of two nucleons with distance

solution_steps.action: verify short range and minimum potential energy distance
solution_steps.explain: potential energy is minimum near 0.8 fm separation; force is repulsive below 0.8 fm and attractive beyond

solution_steps.action: check charge independence and strength relative to Coulomb force
solution_steps.explain: force is identical between p-p, p-n, n-n pairs and much stronger than Coulomb repulsion

concepts.title: Radioactive Decay Types
concepts.definition: Spontaneous emission of alpha particles, beta particles, or gamma rays by unstable atomic nuclei to transform into more stable nuclear configurations.
concepts.key_idea: Radioactivity is a nuclear phenomenon involving emission of matter or electromagnetic radiation.
question_patterns: distinguish between alpha beta and gamma decay modes
what particles or radiation are emitted in radioactive decay
explain the nature of alpha particles emitted by heavy nuclei
describe beta decay process in unstable nuclides
verify conservation of atomic number and mass number in radioactive decay

solution_steps.explain: alpha decay emits helium nuclei, beta decay emits electrons or positrons, gamma decay emits photons
ensure total charge and total nucleon count are conserved across decay equation

concepts.title: Q-Value and Energy Release in Nuclear Fission
concepts.definition: The net energy liberated during a nuclear fission process computed from mass difference between initial reactants and final reaction products.
concepts.key_idea: Nuclear fission releases energy due to higher binding energy per nucleon of intermediate fragments.
question_patterns: calculate the Q value of a nuclear reaction in MeV
find energy released in nuclear fission of heavy nucleus
what is the disintegration energy Q in a fission reaction
determine energy output from mass difference in fission process
compute Q value using reactant and product masses

solution_steps.action: subtract product mass sum from reactant mass sum
solution_steps.explain: find mass defect of reaction in atomic mass units

solution_steps.action: multiply mass difference by energy equivalence constant
solution_steps.explain: convert atomic mass units to MeV energy release

concepts.title: Coulomb Potential Barrier in Nuclear Fusion
concepts.definition: The electrostatic potential energy barrier that two positively charged nuclei must overcome through kinetic energy to undergo fusion.
concepts.key_idea: Mutual electrostatic repulsion creates an energy barrier for fusing nuclei.
question_patterns: calculate the height of the potential barrier for nuclear fusion
find the Coulomb repulsion energy between two touching nuclei
what is the potential energy barrier for two deuterons in contact
determine kinetic energy required to overcome Coulomb barrier
compute potential barrier energy in Joules or electronvolts

solution_steps.action: calculate electrostatic potential energy at contact distance
solution_steps.explain: apply Coulomb potential energy formula for point charges at separation distance

questions: Obtain the binding energy (in MeV) of a nitrogen nucleus 14N, given m(14N) = 14.00307 u.
Obtain the binding energy of the nuclei 56Fe and 209Bi in units of MeV from the following data: m(56Fe) = 55.934939 u and m(209Bi) = 208.980388 u.

A given coin has a mass of 3.0 g. Calculate the nuclear energy that would be required to separate all the neutrons and protons from each other. For simplicity assume that the coin is entirely made of 63Cu atoms (of mass 62.92960 u).
Obtain approximately the ratio of the nuclear radii of the gold isotope 197Au and the silver isotope 107Ag.

The Q value of a nuclear reaction A + b -> C + d is defined by Q = [mA + mb - mC - md] c^2. Determine from the given data the Q-value of the following reactions and state whether the reactions are exothermic or endothermic: (i) 1H + 3H -> 2H + 2H, (ii) 12C + 12C -> 20Ne + 4He.

Suppose we think of fission of a 56Fe nucleus into two equal fragments 28Al. Is the fission energetically possible? Argue by working out Q of the process. Given m(56Fe) = 55.93494 u and m(28Al) = 27.98191 u.

The fission properties of 239Pu are very similar to those of 235U. The average energy released per fission is 180 MeV. How much energy, in MeV, is released if all the atoms in 1 kg of pure 239Pu undergo fission?
How long can an electric lamp of 100W be kept glowing by fusion of 2.0 kg of deuterium? Take the fusion reaction as 2H + 2H -> 3He + n + 3.27 MeV.

Calculate the height of the potential barrier for a head on collision of two deuterons. (Hint: The height of the potential barrier is given by the Coulomb repulsion between the two deuterons when they just touch each other. Assume that they can be taken as hard spheres of radius 2.0 fm.)
From the relation R = R0 * A^(1/3), where R0 is a constant and A is the mass number of a nucleus, show that the nuclear matter density is nearly constant (i.e. independent of A).
